package.question: When a pretrained LLM is given a different tokenizer without any further training, does initializing the unseen-token embeddings with Method M preserve the original model's benchmark performance better than simple and published initialization methods?
package.methods_summary: Method M is a training-free way to swap a pretrained model's tokenizer for a donor model's tokenizer. Tokens shared by both vocabularies act as anchors. For each token that exists only in the donor vocabulary, Method M uses a greedy sparse-approximation algorithm to express the token's donor embedding as a sparse linear combination of k anchor embeddings in the donor model, then applies the same coefficients to the anchors' embeddings in the base model. Baselines: zero vectors (ZeroEmbed), the mean embedding (MeanEmbed), and published methods FOCUS, WECHSEL, CLPTransfer and ZETT, all applied zero-shot without their usual continued training.
package.experimental_setup: Two settings: the Llama 3 vocabulary (about 128k tokens) transplanted into Mistral NeMo 12B (about 131k; about 54% overlap), and the Qwen 2.5 vocabulary (about 152k) transplanted into Llama 3 1B (about 128k; about 86% overlap). Evaluation with the EleutherAI LM Evaluation Harness: MMLU, ARC-Challenge, XNLI, AGIEval, Lambada (zero-shot), GSM8K (5-shot), Belebele, and WikiText bits per byte. The harness's bootstrapped standard errors are about 0.003 to 0.014 for the accuracy metrics (see T1 notes).
